Jamie  following up with the deliverables Rafael promised. Summary here and notes on known regression risks.

Quick recommendations (summary):
- Redwood-XL-8B-quant: strong latency (median ~200ms on hosted GPU), good safety baseline after small refusal tuning. Cost-efficient for high QPS.
- Redwood-2x-13B-int8: higher relevance/accuracy on longer triage flows, recommended for Dedicated if you need fewer hallucinations on long context.

Benchmarks included in the XLS: per-model token cost, median latency (50k-sample sim), 95/99p latency, and safety-refusal metrics on our in-house suite. Key callouts from the safety eval (see safety-eval-samples.pdf):
- Clinical advice prompts: Redwood-XL-8B-quant refuses or provides high-level safe responses in ~92% of cases; failure observed when prompts contain ambiguous multi-step diagnostic asks.
- PHI extraction attempts: baseline models occasionally over-index on pattern extraction; recommend tightening response templates and adding stricter guardrail prompts.

Suggested mitigations we typically implement:
- Response templates + instruction-following fine-tune for non-actionable clinical guidance.
- Prompt-level guardrails: an explicit refusal chain that executes before generation (we included templates in the CSV).
- On-platform monitoring: custom eval hooks to detect regression in refusal rates tied to prompt sets.

Next steps we propose:
- We can run the full prompt set on-hosted Redwood-XL-8B-quant and share full CSV of model outputs by Thu 23 Jul (ETA for full results).
- If you want Dedicated, we can provision a small warm pool and run parallel evals on Redwood-2x-13B-int8 (cost estimate in XLS).

Please see attached files. Happy to hop on a short 30-min readout next week to walk through the XLS and safety findings.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Lead Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
